about.title: Lodi Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision is a shock that doesn't fade on any set schedule, and the legal side of things often feels like an unwelcome intrusion during grief. In Lodi, where reported injury collisions cluster along Cherokee Lane, Kettleman Lane, SR-99, and Lower Sacramento Road, families are sometimes left trying to understand what happened while also managing funeral arrangements and daily life. California law gives a limited group of people the right to bring a wrongful death claim, generally starting with a spouse, domestic partner, or children, and extending to other dependents in certain situations. LawProactive is not a law firm, but we can connect you at no cost with an independent attorney familiar with San Joaquin County courts who can review the circumstances of the crash and explain what recoverable losses may apply to your family's situation, all on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: What You Should Know Before Moving Forward

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases to a spouse, domestic partner, and children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in specific circumstances.

items.title: The Clock Is Shorter Than You Might Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity was involved, so timing matters.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Your Family
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery, so pursuing a claim doesn't add financial strain during an already difficult time.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be able to bring the claim depending on the family situation. An independent attorney can review your circumstances and clarify who qualifies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate proceedings. A criminal case addresses whether the driver broke the law, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action focused on compensating the family for their losses. One can move forward regardless of the outcome of the other.

items.question: Cherokee Lane and SR-99 come up a lot in Lodi crash reports, does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: Public crash-count data for corridors like Cherokee Lane, Kettleman Lane, and SR-99 can provide helpful context, but every case depends on its own facts. An independent attorney will look at the specific collision report, not general area statistics, to evaluate your family's claim.

items.question: What kinds of losses can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: Families may be able to recover funeral and burial costs, lost financial support the deceased would have provided, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. Each family's losses are different, so an attorney can walk through what applies to your situation.
